Naive, bootstrap and multiplier estimates, side by side, and their cost

Source: R/mr_method_tables.R
mr_method_tables.Rd

Plain data frames for the comparison of a forestsearch() analysis's naive estimates with its full-bootstrap and multiplier-resampling corrections, method by method; the caller styles them.

Usage

mr_method_comparison(fits, boots, est.scale = "hr", digits = 2)

mr_cost_table(fits, boots, boot_seconds = NULL, project_B = 1000L)

Arguments

fits

A named list of forestsearch() fits with multiplier resampling and the complement de-biased. The names label the methods.

boots

A list of forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture() results with the same names.

est.scale

"hr" (the default), or "1/hr", which inverts every ratio (limits swap) and is accepted for ratio measures only.

digits

Decimals of the estimates. Default 2.

boot_seconds

The wall-clock seconds of each bootstrap, a vector named by method. NULL (the default) reads what each result stores, the time of its replicate loop (attr(boot$results, "timing")$total_minutes), which leaves out the call's setup and summaries.

project_B

The number of replicates to project the cost to. Default 1000.

Value

mr_method_comparison(): a plain data frame with two rows per method, H and Hc: method, region, n (patients, with their percent), naive (estimate with its robust 95% interval), bootstrap (the point estimate), and multiplier (the two-term de-biased estimate with its IJ 95% interval). The interval reads NA on a fit whose stored limits are not the two-term IJ interval; see mr_values().

mr_cost_table(): a plain data frame with one row per method: method, mr_seconds, bootstrap_B, bootstrap_seconds, seconds_per_replicate, and projected_B_<project_B>.

Details

What the comparison shows. The table compares displays; it does not adjudicate one quantity. The bootstrap column carries the point estimate only: at a small B that point is an illustration, and its interval is not a result. For families generated from a model (the DINA and GRF paths), the full bootstrap, which re-runs the search in every replicate, and multiplier resampling, which perturbs one fixed family, target different estimands.

mr_cost_table()'s mr_seconds is the multiplier stage as the fit records it (mr_inference$timing_seconds), and the projection is linear in B at the worker count the bootstrap ran on.

See also

mr_values(), mr_estimates_table(), forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture().

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n <- 500
d <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n), treat = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5), x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
d$time <- rexp(n, 0.1 * ifelse(d$treat == 1, ifelse(d$x1 < -0.6, 3, 0.45), 1))
d$event <- as.integer(d$time < 30)
d$time <- pmin(d$time, 30)
fit <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = d, outcome.name = "time", event.name = "event", treat.name = "treat",
  id.name = "id", confounders.name = c("x1", "x2"), use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE,
  maxk = 1, fs.splits = 200, sg_focus = "hrMaxSG", mr_inference = TRUE,
  mr_inference_args = list(draws = 200, field_R_out = 50, field_R_in = 25),
  parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"), quiet = TRUE, details = FALSE,
  plot.sg = FALSE, show_candidate_summary = FALSE)
boot <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(fit, nb_boots = 2,
                                        parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential"))
#> Warning: nb_boots < 100 may produce unreliable confidence intervals. Recommend at least 500 for production use.
#> Bootstrap parallel config: Using user-provided settings
#> System max cores available: 4
#> Bootstrap will use:  workers with 'sequential' plan
#> Bootstrap iteration 1/2
#> Bootstrap iteration 2/2
mr_method_comparison(list(FS = fit), list(FS = boot))
#>   method region         n             naive bootstrap        multiplier
#> 1     FS      H 134 (27%) 3.56 (2.45, 5.16)      5.07 3.62 (1.50, 8.74)
#> 2     FS     Hc 366 (73%) 0.54 (0.43, 0.67)      0.58 0.52 (0.29, 0.93)
mr_cost_table(list(FS = fit), list(FS = boot))
#>   method mr_seconds bootstrap_B bootstrap_seconds seconds_per_replicate
#> 1     FS      0.007           2              3.48                  1.74
#>   projected_B_1000
#> 1             1740
# }
